newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy govt wins confidence vote on dairy decree.
newsitem.headline: Italy govt wins confidence vote on dairy decree.

text.p: The Italian government on Tuesday won a confidence motion in the Chamber of Deputies (lower house) on a decree to reform the milk sector.
The centre-left government won the do-or-die measure by 308 votes to 223 with no abstentions, parliamentary officials said.

The decree, which is due to pass to the Senate (upper house) for further ratification relates to a package of reforms for the dairy sector, which has been hit by a bitter dispute with farmers over strict European Union quotas.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi's government unveiled the decree, containing emergency aid measures for the sector, in January after farmers blockaded roads and airports for two weeks in protest at hefty EU overproduction fines.
The farmers had accused the state of failing to advise them of their correct quotas and initially refused to pay.

The government responded with the bill, which offered cheap loans and payments by instalment plus a pledge to set up a commission to examine the farmers' grievances. Italy has also asked the European Commission to increase its milk quotas.
The confidence vote was called over a government amendment to the decree and includes changes to the text of the bill. The government would have had to resign if it had lost the vote.

The European Commission decided earlier this month to withold farm funds from Italy, Spain and Greece for failing to pay the so-called EU super-levy fines for overshooting their 1995-96 milk output quotas.
Italian farmers were fined 192.2 million Ecus ($167 million). They have made a partial payment.
Agriculture Minister Michele Pinto survived a no-confidence vote last month after opposition parties tried to oust him for his handling of the milk crisis.

Decree laws issued by the government have force for only 60 days unless approved within that time by parliament. They cannot be re-issued and Prodi has called several confidence votes to push through legislation. He has survived them all comfortably.
The milk decree expires on April 1.
